title: Joe Lutcher takes a tape to Dave Dexter
summary: Joe, trying to get started, took a home tape to Dave Dexter, who liked the voice but never passed the message on.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: Record labels, producers and the business of making albums

blocks.x: We haven't talked about Joe very much, except that he was up at Capitol and talking to Dave Dexter before you were discovered. Was he up at Capitol because he was recording for Capitol then?

No. He did record with Capitol later, but at the time he was trying to get started, and of course he was the type to go around to different people doing what you have to do, you know. You've got to go knock on doors. I never was much of a door knocker, door rapper. But he went to several places, of course, and he was writing. He always did write. He was a marvelous arranger. And he was trying to get started and get something going. So at the time he went up to see Dave Dexter, he had a little -- I don't remember what it was now, but some little something that he had done. I had a little home tape recorder, and I used to do things, you know, at home. And whatever this was, he took it up to Dave Dexter and Dave heard it and he said he -- whatever the material was, he didn't

particularly like the song or whatever, but he liked the voice and he mentioned to Joe that he wanted -- he said, 'I'd like to get in touch with your sister. Maybe we can do something, you know, something else, submit some other material or something, and have her to get in touch with me.' Well, Joe, I don't know, probably he forgot about it, but he never did mention it to me, and it probably wasn't important, or he didn't think it was maybe important at the time. But later, when I was on the March of Dimes Show, I think which we discussed earlier, that's when Dexter heard me, so it all started from that.
